newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Creditors demand resignation of Kia Group execs.
newsitem.headline: Creditors demand resignation of Kia Group execs.

text.p: A Korea First Bank executive said on Wednesday creditors of the Kia Group had demanded the group's current executives resign unconditionally.
Korea First Bank director Lee Ho-keun told a news conference creditors also demanded Asia Motors Corp be sold off, rather than absorbed by Kia Motors Corp as proposed by the group.
Kim Sun-hong, chairman of the nation's eighth-largest conglomerate, had proposed that the group's management would resign if its self-rescue plans fail.
Korea First is the biggest commercial bank among creditors of the Kia Group, which earlier this month was selected by creditors for bail-out.
The news conference was organised after creditors ended without decision a meeting that had been expected to yield details of the creditors' bail-out plan.
Lee said Kia's management would have to present a written promise for an unconditional resignation before Friday when creditors will meet again.
"If Kia wants to get emergency loans, it should turn over a memorandum promising the management's unconditional resignation before Friday," said Lee.
The meeting was also due to review a Korea First Bank proposal of extending 183.1 billion won to four of Kia's affiliates, including flagship Kia Motors Corp.

Lee said creditors expressed worries that absorption of Asia Motors, proposed as part of the group's plan to sell off, merge or spin off 23 of its 28 domestic affiliates, could worsen the financial status of Kia Motors.
Creditors also demanded Kia supplement already proposed self-rescue plans that include the reduction of workforce and sales of idle real estate, Lee said.
Kia was the third conglomerate tapped for protection under a voluntary committee formed by major banks in April to prevent promising companies from going bankrupt.
The two others were the Jinro and Dainong groups.
